programmes.d: In 1989, the dead bodies of Joan Rogers and her two teenage daughters were found floating in Tampa Bay.
Doctors cannot pinpoint the source of a businessman's illness.
On the night of May 22, 1992, Betty Wilson returned home after a meeting and discovered her husband lying in a pool of blood. Jack Wilson had obviously been murdered — but how?
After 6-year-old Michelle Lee Dorr went missing, her father confessed to murdering her.

Seattle police had no suspects in the violent murder of grunge singer Mia Zapata. More than a decade passed before evidence collected by a prescient medical examiner could be used by forensic scientists to identify the killer.
The 1996 investigation into 48-year-old Martha Hansen's murder is helped by a legal requirement.

Susie Mowbray was charged in her husband's death. Her son was so convinced of her innocence that he enrolled in law school, studied all of the evidence and, eventually, discovered the truth of what really happened between his parents.
The disappearance of a mail-order bride is suspicious when police learn of the husband's past wives.
Two sets of scientists probe a woman's death.
A jeweler's search through old sales records helps police find likely suspects in a couple's murder.
In a 1992 murder case, the autopsy of a cremated body turns up telltale clues of foul play.
Garbage bag leads to a killer.

Robert Sims returns home after working the night shift and finds his wife unconscious on the kitchen floor. Their son is fast asleep in an upstairs bedroom, but their six-week-old daughter, Heather, is missing.
An investigation into the murder of Katie Poirier is stymied by the lack of a body.

Rachael Mullenix, 19, was convicted of stabbing her mother, Barbara Mullenix, in 2006. She allegedly packed her mother's bloodied corpse in a cardboard box before dumping it in California's Newport Bay.
The sensitive nose of a forensic examiner sniffs out murder.
A mother of two vanishes after a shopping trip. Her body is discovered a month later, and witnesses say they saw the victim being forced into a car by an unknown person.
An assailant avoids the law for 16 years due to a lack of evidence.

The victim had been sexually assaulted and stabbed to death on the beach. A pair of men's tennis shoes was discovered near her body. Police were sure that if they found the man who fit the shoes, they would also find the man who committed the crime.
The only clue recovered from a shooting is a twelve-guage shotgun.

In this classic episode of Forensic Files, the longest-running true crime series in television history, Eileen and Derrick Severs disappear from their home in a small village in Great Britain and police find evidence of foul play.
A serial arsonist starts several fires that cause the deaths of three people.
A Modesto, California teenager goes missing. With no signs of struggle in her home, police suspect she has simply run away — until her naked, bruised body is discovered in a ditch 20 miles away.
Computers aid the police and FBI in solving a string of crimes in St. Louis.
When a talented television news anchor is shot to death outside her home, it appears to be a crime of passion perpetrated by an obsessed fan.
Using an anonymous letter and geographical profiling, investigators close in on a serial rapist.
In 1995, when off-duty Maine State Trooper Vicky Gardner is attacked by Steven Fortin during a routine stop, it triggers a chain of events which jumpstart a stalled murder case in New Jersey.
A three-year-old develops a respiratory condition. His father has Alzheimers.
Mark Fair left for work and his fiancée, Karla Brown, stayed home. Later, he found her dead. During the autopsy, bite marks on her body were re-examined and forensic odontology identified the killer.
A murder investigation in Florida crosses jurisdictions from New York and Jamaica.
When a college student vanished without a trace, her fellow students were concerned about her safety and their own.
An examination of the 2002 DC area shooting spree that resulted in ten murders.
A woman convicted of killing her mother in a car fire is granted a new trial.

A young woman is found dead in her apartment. With little evidence at the scene, the case turns cold — until police discover a link between their prime suspect and an unsolved murder committed six years earlier in a different state.
Notepad points to kidnapper.

An obstetrician returned home from the hospital and found his wife on the bathroom floor. She was covered with blood and not breathing. He tried unsuccessfully to revive her, staining his clothes with her blood in the process.
Debate over cause of death.

Avis Banks and her unborn child were brutally murdered. The body was discovered by her fiancé, Keyon Pittman. When police learned that Pittman was having affairs with other women, he became the prime suspect.
A killer leaves the scene with the genetic fingerprint of his victim.

A woman disappears without a trace. Even though foul play is suspected, the leads don't pan out and the trail turns cold. Twenty years would pass before police are able to link a clump of hair discovered in an isolated area with the missing woman.
A vacuum-cleaner bag of microscopic paint-particles helps to identify a killer.
This episode documents a deadly bombing at a church in Oakwood, Illinois, in December 1997.
A mother of two vanishes after a shopping trip. Her body is discovered a month later.
A serial rapist is on the loose in a Texas town. No one knew where he'd strike next, but the audacity of his attacks and the escalation of violence against his victims made finding him imperative.
A physics professor and NASA technology help to catch a killer.
By using techniques she saw on forensic science TV shows, a mother determines who was responsible for the accident that permanently injured her 4-year-old daughter.
In 1993, worldwide attention focused on robberies which targeted tourists in Florida.
A young woman is stabbed more than 100 times. The killer leaves DNA behind, but investigators must play a cat-and-mouse game to obtain a suspect's DNA to match.
At a murder scene, investigators find a shoe-print, several foreign hairs and unknown fingerprints.

Police suspect Dr. John "Jack" Boyle in the disappearance of his wife, Noreen, when he signs mortgage papers for a new house with a woman pretending to be his spouse. The police later find Noreen's body in the basement of Dr. Boyle's new house.
A death in Pennsylvania is strikingly similar to one in North Carolina.
Two eyewitnesses may hold the key to the death of a motorcycle gang member.
A nurse learns that she has been deliberately infected with HIV.
While skeet shooting on a beautiful spring day, Martin Dillon is shot dead. His friend maintains it was a freak accident, but it takes more than 20 years for the truth to surface.
A pregnant woman is found murdered in her air-conditioned bedroom.

It was the single most deadly automobile accident in American history. Almost a hundred vehicles were involved, twelve people died and more than fifty people were injured. And it happened along a stretch of highway long known for dense, thick fog.
Police were puzzled by an obscure print found at a murder crime scene.
When a hit-and-run accident claimed the life of a high school athlete, everyone in town mourned his passing. Finding the killer was a long shot at best.
A man is found dead in his home and his ex-wife has an almost perfect alibi.
Who was the sexual offender who murdered two adolescent boys in Nebraska? The key to stopping him would be the unique composition of the "junk rope" he used to tie his victims.
A union official is executed in his home not long after a strike by the union membership.

In 2002, funeral director Lonnie Turner, Sr. was found shot to death. His son Lonnie Jr. became the prime suspect, particularly after it was discovered that the murder was committed with his gun. However, he had an alibi for the time of the murder.
In 1988, the body of a young woman was discovered in an Ohio river.
Crystal Faye Todd's case is examined; the popular high school student was raped and murdered.

The body of a wealthy American businessman was found in his rental car. Teeth and bone fragments were the only remains. When the victim's wife files an insurance claim for $7 million, investigators seek the help of a renowned forensic anthropologist.
Police discovered the body of Douglas Beamish's estranged wife.
Young Navajos in the Southwest were dying at an alarming rate. The tribe's medicine men provided investigators with a critical clue that would lead halfway around the world to a most unlikely killer.
More than 700 Oregonians contracted food poisoning from a unique strain of salmonella in 1984.

A two-man shrimp boat sinks when a fast-moving, violent storm strikes the Louisiana coast. The captain drowns, but the deckhand is rescued fourteen hours later. The crewman is hailed as a hero — until the captain's body is discovered.
A woman is found dead from a gunshot wound and police suspect her husband.

In 1994, a human skull retrieved from an Ohio pond reveals a ghastly crime. Markings on the skull indicate that the victim had been stabbed multiple times and that the teeth had been removed with needle-nose pliers.
In 1995, the founder of American Atheists disappeared with $500,000 in gold coins.

When a woman disappeared without a trace, there were two possible explanations: kidnapping or murder. Careful investigation, a forensic artist and DNA profiling enabled police to find a single suspect, who was known to prey upon vulnerable women.
Two eyewitnesses may hold the key to the death of a motorcycle gang member.
A murder investigation in Florida crosses jurisdictions from New York and Jamaica. The police rely on cell phone mapping, wiretapping and a host of forensic evidence to link a suspect to a murder.
In 1984, a passerby finds the torso of a woman in a cardboard box.

When convenience store employee Wanda Mason is found dead, investigators find the entire murder has been caught on the store's security camera. But the image of the killer is so degraded it seems impossible to positively identify him.
A victim's knowledge of forensic evidence leads police to her abductor.

A woman is reported missing after a fight with her husband. Police suspect a man who reported a fire in his car. Two tiny drops of blood are found in the interior. Finally, a tiny clue inside the suspect's watchband helps solve the case.
The police investigate when a severed leg is discovered among garbage.
When court clerk Peter Porco doesn't report to work in November 2004, a courts officer is ordered to the Porcos' family home in Bethlehem, NY.
In a 1992 murder case, the autopsy of a cremated body turns up telltale clues of foul play.

When Joann Katrinak is found dead in a corn field with her infant son, the obvious suspect is the husband and father of the victims. But insects found on the bodies reveal a vital clue which uncovers a twisted story of passion gone wrong.
Forensic developments reveal new facts in the case of a man convicted of sexual assault.

When a fire destroyed most of a home and a young boy went missing, police organized the largest search in the history of their small town. First the boy's backpack was discovered five miles from home, then his body was found 50 miles away.
The murder of a couple puzzles investigators until the victims' dog leads police to the killer.
After inspecting storm damage to a home in Tampa, an insurance assessor simply disappeared. Thirty hours later, her body was found in a nearby river. But the killer had been careless.
Soon after becoming pregnant, firefighter Michelle Baker's health quickly deteriorates.
While investigating the apparent overdose suicide of Reverend Bill Guthrie's wife, detectives recover incriminating files from Bill's computer and learn of his infidelity.
In the 1980s, a trio of unsolved murders occurred in Wichita Falls, Texas.

In this international case of extortion, murder and stolen identities, scam-artist Albert J. Walker assumes the identity of co-worker Ronald Platt. Platt later turns up dead in an ocean with an anchor tied around his torso.
An abandoned, still-running car leads investigators to a body with unusual marks.
On May 12, 1994, Crystal Perry was viciously murdered in her home in Bridgton, Maine. Michael Hutchinson, 32, was later found guilty in the slaying.
Police uncover deleted computer files during an investigation.

A man disappears one year to the day after beginning an affair with his friend's wife. 15 years later, with the help of a metal detector, police find evidence that would prove what had happened and who was responsible.
A suspicious neighbor gives police a break in a cold case.

When two women from the same town were murdered in the same way, police feared a serial killer was on the loose. At first they thought the victims had nothing in common until they found tiny clues linking them to the same man.
The 1987 disappearance of Houston resident Tracy Jo Shine is recalled.

The doctors at the hospital couldn't determine the cause of Bobby Curley's hallucinations and intense pain. They treated it as a neurological disorder but his condition deteriorated. He was being poisoned.
Doctors cannot pinpoint the source of a businessman's illness.
